title: 3 Needles
full_review:
"3 Needles" (Wolfe) is an epic three-part drama about the worldwide spread of AIDS through poverty, indifference, ignorance, irresponsibility and greed told through three narratives.

In the Chinese story, a contraband blood dealer, Jin Ping (Lucy Liu), sells tainted blood, and a poor farmer, Tong Sam (Tanabadee Chokpikultong), tries to get to the bottom of the sickness mysteriously affecting his family and villagers.

In Montreal, porn actor Denny (Shawn Ashmore) passes off his father's blood as his own to avoid HIV detection, while his wily mother, Olive (Stockard Channing), indulges in a fraudulent scheme.

Finally, in South Africa, Sister Clara (Chloe Sevigny), a novice, and the others in a community of nuns, including Sister Hilde (Olympia Dukakis) and Sister Mary (Sandra Oh), try to educate and convert the locals dying of the disease.

Director Thom Fitzgerald's cautionary tale is majestically photographed and, on the whole, absorbing, though marred by several lurid plot elements (at one point, Sister Clara gives in to the sexual demands of a plantation owner, played by Ian Roberts, in return for improved conditions for the people). Unlike many of today's multistory films, this one's stories are not interconnected, and overall the film would have benefited from a sharper focus.

Worthy as the consciousness-raising aspects of the film are, the flagged items below -- however dramatically sound and discreetly presented -- may limit the film's appeal to Catholic viewers.

The film contains full indigenous male and partial female nudity, a circumcision, sexual encounters and multiple rapes, brief pornographic tableaux without nudity, condom use, drug references, some profanity and rough language, and a graphic childbirth scene.

Multiple languages and partly subtitled. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. It is not rated by the Motion Picture Association of America.
